original_question: On which chromosome is the gene encoding phosphatidylcholine-sterol O-acyltransferase, whose deficiency leads to fish-eye disease characterized by symptoms such as corneal opacity, anemia, and kidney damage, located?

final_qi.question: On which chromosome is the gene encoding phosphatidylcholine-sterol O-acyltransferase, whose deficiency leads to fish-eye disease characterized by symptoms such as corneal opacity, anemia, and kidney damage, located?
final_qi.long_answer: Fish-eye disease is caused by partial deficiency of lecithin–cholesterol acyltransferase (phosphatidylcholine-sterol O-acyltransferase). The human LCAT gene that encodes this enzyme has been mapped to the long arm of chromosome 16 (16q22). Pathogenic variants in this gene impair cholesterol esterification, producing the characteristic corneal opacity, anemia, and renal damage seen in fish-eye disease.

final_answer.long_answer: Fish-eye disease results from deficiency of the enzyme phosphatidylcholine-sterol O-acyltransferase, encoded by the LCAT gene. In humans the LCAT gene is mapped to the long arm of chromosome 16 (16q22.1); mutations here impair cholesterol esterification, producing the corneal opacity, hemolytic anemia, and renal involvement characteristic of the disorder.
